notes.text: Bowen Byram is day to day (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 34% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 80:55 together, down from 47% with Byram.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Yanni Gourde is on the injured non-roster list (hip surgery) and has not played this season.
Erik Černák is day to day and missed their last game. J.J. Moser has taken his spot beside Ryan McDonagh.
Max Crozier returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

story.head: Mikheyev meets his old team
paras: The Blackhawks (4-9-1) lost 5-4 in overtime to Boston on Saturday, and the Lightning (8-3-2) lost 5-4 in a shootout to Nashville the same night. The Blackhawks played last night, and the Lightning are rested. Going in, the Blackhawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Bolts fourth in the Atlantic (tied for eighth).

The Blackhawks have played better than their record (.321) says: their chances are worth about .384, and their finishing has held them back. The Lightning’s record (.692) is about what their chances are worth.

The Blackhawks pick their shots (2nd lowest), don't block many shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (31st). Chicago has scored 2.21 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.79, the third most. As for the Lightning, they ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd), get into a lot of chippy games (3rd) and let the point shots come and guard the net (4th). The Lightning are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blackhawks. On top of that, the Lightning could find some good looks against the Blackhawks, who give up plenty of them.

Connor Bedard (4 G / 5 A / 9 P in 8 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (5 G / 2 A / 7 P in 14 GP) has a team-high five goals. For the Lightning, Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Chicago. Brandon Hagel (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Arvid Söderblom (0-2-1 / .829 SV% in 3 GS) will likely start for Chicago, and Andrei Vasilevskiy (6-3-1 / .877 SV% in 10 GS) for Tampa Bay.

At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Hagel, Cirelli and Holmberg out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kantserov, Bedard and Donato. Elsewhere, the Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.

The Blackhawks have been without Bowen Byram since Oct 13.
The Lightning are newly without Erik Černák, and have had to make do without Yanni Gourde all season.
Brayden Point has three goals on chances worth about 5.6 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
